previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease was admitted for fatigue, weakness, and lethargy following recent hand surgery and an active flare of microscopic colitis. She had been consuming minimal nutrition, mostly broth, and presented with symptoms concerning for adrenal insufficiency. Initial labs showed mild hyponatremia and elevated creatinine, consistent with dehydration. She received IV fluids overnight, which improved her kidney function and clinical status. Her symptoms resolved, and she was not in adrenal crisis. She was discharged the following day with temporary doubling of fludrocortisone and prednisone for three days, new prescriptions for calcium citrate and vitamin D, and instructions to hold metoprolol until steroid tapering was complete. Follow-up was arranged with endocrinology to reassess electrolytes and medication dosing.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
